original_pre_race_assessment.raw_reasoning:
His Worcester chase debut fourth was 6 lengths behind with early keenness and late jumping errors. Inside Man has a recent 4-length Chepstow second on good ground; Sweeper System won a 2m chase at Worcester after improving from his debut. Those are demonstrated chase routes against Jamada's still-needed improvement.

Jamada was returning after five months, finished with promise, is down from OR108 to107 and has Olly Murphy/Sean Bowen. Experience can improve settling and jumping. His 155 lb is the lowest declared weight; that positive is genuine.

Retain as a racing candidate, below Top Guy and East India Express. The opposition can already perform credibly over fences; the case does not require three hypothetical improvements. Price 1000.00 rejected.

Inside Man's 10 lb higher rating is fully paid for by 10 lb more weight (165 versus155); no free ratings advantage. He also made jumping errors at Chepstow. Sweeper System is 5 lb higher after winning and at156 lb has no obvious handicap gift. Black Hawk Eagle drops in grade but was 17 lengths behind Inside Man's winner in the same Chepstow race and carries168; this is a revival route ranked third. Yes Indeed is on a reduced mark; Homme D'Un Soir returns to chasing after a poor hurdle effort; Granny Hawkins debuts over fences after losing form. None is silently excluded.

More reliable execution by Inside Man or Sweeper System defeats Jamada while he remains inexperienced. If he is beaten by a different revival horse, record broad competition rather than crediting the principal ranking.

[Verified racecard](https://www.sportinglife.com/racing/racecards/2026-11-23/kempton/racecard/949840/copybet-follow-us-on-x-lilies-mares-hurdle-listed-gbb-race). Five runners all active; Good;2m5f Listed hurdle. Original ranked rivals for this new proposal: **1 Take No Chances,2 Hollygrove Cha Cha,3 St Irene**. La Pinsonniere is reviewed below, not ignored. API race `rac_32305250562`, horse `hrs_40352494`.

**Demonstrated competition:** Take No Chances146/154 versus Jackie130/154 is an uncompensated16 lb ratings difference in a non-handicap. Her Wetherby Grade 2 third was1.75 lengths behind Strong Leader on Good, following an Aintree Grade 1 second over3m1f. She has current-season fitness and tactical versatility; no guarantee of a repeat. Hollygrove140/158 is a Listed hurdle winner at a similar trip, with a plausible uncontested lead: her4 lb extra weight offsets only part of a10 lb ratings gap to Jackie. These are two specific established winning routes.

**Strongest winning case:** Jackie won twice over hurdles last season and improved to fifth in the Grade 2 Dawn Run, beaten only 5.75 lengths on Good, finishing strongly after pressure. That is a respectable performance, not a failure merely because fifth. She then finished sixth in a Fairyhouse Grade 1,18.75 lengths behind on Soft. She is6, lightly raced over hurdles and can progress beyond OR 130 returning after 232 days for Harry Derham/Jonathan Burke. Absence is not proof of unfitness; her stable’s recent2/11 record is a contextual positive, not a probability.

**Why the decision survives:** The novice improvement is real, but current evidence does not establish the required leap over an experienced146-rated rival at identical weight, plus a140-rated proven Listed winner carrying only 4 lb more. At favouritism, she is the clearest subject to oppose in this race on demonstrated competition. This is the strong-competition route, not two invented ability faults. The additional historical review confirms the distinction between respectable novice form and proven superiority over these opponents.

**Limits:** Take No Chances has not won recently and her tactical speed over2m5f is not guaranteed; the3m Wetherby result must not be treated as an identical race. Hollygrove can regress or lack sharpness after her absence, and most wins were on soft/heavy; do not call Good unsuitable without evidence. St Irene’s127 rating at 156 lb leaves her below Jackie on these terms; her step up in trip is only a secondary improvement route. La Pinsonniere126/154 has a useful C&D third but poor recent form and first-time blinkers; no unverified revival assumed.

**Mechanism to test:** A named established mare, chiefly Take No Chances or Hollygrove, beats Jackie through demonstrated ability on favourable level-race terms. A lay success through a casualty or an unexpected outsider would not validate the full mechanism. If Jackie improves and wins, record that the recognised improvement case prevailed. No retrospective change to this reasoning or ranks.

Opposition is established at this track and 6f. Wise Crack won over C&D on 6 November despite a stumbled start and traffic; Storm Esme won over C&D in September and was second, beaten 1 length, in a Class5 here on 30 October; Noelies Dream was half a length behind Wise Crack. These form lines provide multiple concrete routes.

Encore won a 6f Kempton novice and narrowly missed in a 7f Southwell handicap. The subsequent 6f seventh had a genuine wide/no-cover explanation and came in Class4, while today is Class5. She is on OR70, the same mark as her close second, and Haggas/Fallon is a credible revival combination. That run is not treated as a conclusive decline.

Retain a strong-competition racing candidate, the least forceful of these four. The case rests on the current C&D opposition after allowing for a plausible revival, not on turning an excusable run into two negatives. Price 1000.00 rejected.

Encore135 lb/OR70 versus Wise Crack132/67, Storm Esme133/68 and Noelies Dream132/67 are broadly normal handicap terms, not automatic weight advantages. Wise Crack is up4 lb; Noelies Dream meets him 2 lb better for a half-length, so their order can reverse. The Green Man is a genuine fourth-ranked course revival route but starts slowly. Spun To Gold's recent third and 5 lb claim merit consideration, without treating a 5f placing as identical 6f evidence. The other four have current form/trip/headgear uncertainties.

A named C&D performer supplies the winning route against Encore's revival. If she rebounds and wins, retain the failed judgement and acknowledge that her known class-drop and excuse were insufficiently offset.

Wise Crack won over C&D on 6 November despite a stumbled start and traffic; Storm Esme won over C&D in September and was second, beaten 1 length, in a Class5 here on 30 October; Noelies Dream was half a length behind Wise Crack. These form lines provide multiple concrete routes. Encore135 lb/OR70 versus Wise Crack132/67, Storm Esme133/68 and Noelies Dream132/67 are broadly normal handicap terms, not automatic weight advantages. Wise Crack is up4 lb; Noelies Dream meets him 2 lb better for a half-length, so their order can reverse. The Green Man is a genuine fourth-ranked course revival route but starts slowly. Spun To Gold's recent third and 5 lb claim merit consideration, without treating a 5f placing as identical 6f evidence. The other four have current form/trip/headgear uncertainties.

post_race_observations.analysis: Ninth; original rank2 Storm Esme won, rank1 Wise Crack sixth and rank3 Noelies Dream tenth. Encore was slowly away, keen, made an effort over two furlongs out and lost position over one furlong out. The named course-and-distance opposition supplied the winning route despite Encore’s plausible revival. This does not prove that her previous wide/no-cover excuse was false or that the class drop could never work. No cumulative beaten margin is asserted: the current stored parser leaves it unknown after the dead-heat for fourth.
